subject: Prorated pack conversion / legacy discount preservation — redlines
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Ellis <naomi@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: pack conversion approach + legacy discount preservation

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for walking through Beacon's move from monthly packs to usage-based billing. Per our call, attached is a draft of the pricing exhibit that maps legacy packs to equivalent usage bands and shows how discounts would carry over for existing customers. High-level notes: 

- We propose prorating any partial-month packs at conversion date, crediting leftover value to the first two billing cycles in USD credits.
- For customers on legacy multi-month discounts (e.g., 10% on 12-month packs), Redwood is proposing a 12-month preservation window where the equivalent annual discount is applied as a blended consumption credit.
- We added a \"legacy discount preservation\" clause (Section 3.2) that preserves discount percentage but not the pack commit minimums — this is to avoid locking Beacon into minimums that no longer align to usage patterns.

Can you confirm whether Beacon needs a hard guarantee (contractual) for the preserved discount or whether a billing credit in the first year is sufficient? Legal asks for clarity on that point before we circulate redlines.

I’ve cc'd Karthik and Laura from our deal/legal ops team to weigh in on implementation and the proposed language. I also attached a mapping spreadsheet showing several conversion scenarios.

Next steps we’d like:
- Beacon to confirm preferred treatment (contractual amendment vs billing credit) by 10/06
- If contractual, we’ll circulate a short amendment to Exhibit B with the preservation clause and a sample true-up matrix.

Thanks — we want to make the transition low-friction for your finance team.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: pricing-conversion-mapping.xlsx)
From: Naomi Ellis <naomi@beaconhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@beaconhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: pack conversion approach + legacy discount preservation

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear write-up. Quick answers from our side:

1) Beacon prefers a contractual guarantee for the portion of discount tied to prior committed spend that existed as of the conversion date. Finance wants the protection in writing (so not just a post-hoc credit).
2) We agree that removing hard minimums is okay as long as the preserved discount is timebound (12 months is acceptable).
3) Procurement would like a clause that prevents the preserved discount from applying to any add-on SKUs purchased after the conversion date — only legacy SKUs get the carryover.

I'm looping in procure@beaconhealth.com for legal and SOW alignment. Can your legal ops draft the amendment language? We'll review and aim to return redlines within 4 business days.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Ellis
Director, Cloud Ops
Beacon Health
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: internal: proposed amendment language + risk notes

Jordan / Laura —

I reviewed Beacon's ask (contractual guarantee for preserved discount on legacy committed spend). Drafted a short amendment to Exhibit B that: 

- Adds a defined term "Legacy Commitment" (stores the dollar value/units as of conversion date).
- Provides a 12-month "Preservation Period" during which the equivalent discount percentage is applied to charges attributable to usage mapped from the Legacy Commitment.
- Explicitly excludes add-on SKUs and future purchases (per Beacon request).
- Includes an audit-rights paragraph limited to quarterly validation (read-only ledger access or reconciled reports) — legal insists on narrow scope to avoid broad data requests.
- Includes a fallback "billing credit" mechanism if a post-conversion true-up shows the customer effectively used less than historical commitment — this avoids over-crediting.

Risk/ops notes: the audit-rights + the preservation metric will require a mapping function we already built in the spreadsheet. Implementation will need 2 weeks of billing engineering time to wire the true-up and credit path. If Beacon demands more granularity in audit access, we should push back or propose a controlled API feed rather than raw ledger access.

I attached a redline PDF (Beacon_Exhibit_Price_Conversion_redline_20261009.pdf) for Jordan to send to Beacon once we agree. Also adding language suggestions below for quick copy/paste into DocuSign: 

"During the twelve (12) month Preservation Period following the Conversion Date, Redwood shall apply the Legacy Discount Percentage to charges attributable to volumes mapped to the Legacy Commitment. Charges for add-on SKUs or products not included in the Legacy Commitment are excluded from Preservation. The parties shall reconcile usage quarterly and execute a true-up resulting in a billing credit if actual usage associated with mapped volumes is less than the credited amount."

Flagging for LAURA: is the phrase "attributable to volumes mapped to the Legacy Commitment" sufficiently tight for legal? If not, propose additions.

Karthik
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Ellis <naomi@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, procure@beaconhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-09T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: pack conversion approach + legacy discount preservation — redlines

Naomi —

Thanks — attached is the redline we discussed (Beacon_Exhibit_Price_Conversion_redline_20261009.pdf). Key updates per your asks:

- Contractual Preservation: added defined "Legacy Commitment" and 12-month Preservation Period with explicit guarantee language.
- Scope: exclusion language for add-on SKUs included.
- Audit: limited, quarterly reconciliation rights (read-only reports or agreed extracts).
- True-up: billing credit fallback and reconciliation cadence spelled out.

If Beacon is good with the language as-is, we can prepare a short amendment (Exhibit B - Pricing) for signature and target an effective Conversion Date of 10/15/2026. If you want any tightening around mapping rules, Laura is our point for legal tweaks (cc'd).

Would you like us to share a DocuSign packet or send to your procurement portal?

Best,
Jordan
(attachment: Beacon_Exhibit_Price_Conversion_redline_20261009.pdf, pricing-conversion-mapping.xlsx)
